{{short description|Iranian-Swedish mathematician}}
'''Sara Zahedi''' (born 1981 in [[Tehran]])<ref name="em"/> is an [[Iranian peoples|Iranian]]-[[Swedes|Swedish]] [[mathematician]] who works in [[computational fluid dynamics]] and holds a professorship in [[numerical analysis]] at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] (KTH) in [[Sweden]]. She is one of ten winners and the only female winner of the [[European Mathematical Society]] Prize for 2016 "for her outstanding research regarding the development and analysis of [[Numerical analysis|numerical algorithms]] for [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]] with a focus on applications to problems with dynamically changing [[geometry]]". The topic of Zahedi's EMS Prize lecture was her recent research on the CutFEM method of solving [[fluid dynamics]] problems with changing boundary geometry, such as arise when simulating the dynamics of systems of two immiscible liquids.<ref name="7ecm">[http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/system/files/news/Druck%20-%20pp_3657_Broschuere%20-%207ECM.pdf Prize laureates] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006190620/http://euro-math-soc.eu/system/files/news/Druck%20-%20pp_3657_Broschuere%20-%207ECM.pdf |date=2018-10-06 }}, 7th Eur. Congress of Mathematics, July 18–22, 2016, retrieved 2016-07-26.</ref> This method combines [[level set method]]s to represent the domain boundaries as cuts through an underlying uniform grid, together with numerical simulation techniques that can adapt to the complex geometries of grid cells cut by these boundaries.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Burman | first1 = Erik
 | last2 = Claus | first2 = Susanne
 | last3 = Hansbo | first3 = Peter
 | last4 = Larson | first4 = Mats G.
 | last5 = Massing | first5 = André
 | date = December 2014
 | doi = 10.1002/nme.4823
 | issue = 7
 | journal = International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering
 | pages = 472–501
 | title = CutFEM: Discretizing geometry and partial differential equations
 | volume = 104| bibcode = 2015IJNME.104..472B| url = http://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1471066/1/Burman%20et%20al.%20CutFEM%20Discretizing%20geometry%20.pdf
 | doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>

When Zahedi was ten years old, with her father having been killed by the regime after the [[Iranian Revolution]], her mother sent her on her own as a refugee to Sweden, and only rejoined her some years later.<ref name="em">{{citation|url=http://www.elmundo.es/ciencia/2016/07/20/578f3a0de5fdea4d558b459c.html|title=Me gusta resolver problemas matemáticos del mundo real: Sara Zahedi, del Royal Institute of Technology (Suecia), ganadora del premio EMS a matemáticos jóvenes|language=Spanish|first=Ágata|last=Timon|date=July 20, 2016|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]}}.</ref><ref name="dw">{{citation|title=A refugee's story: 'Math was a language I understood'|date=July 18, 2016|work=Don't call me a prodigy: the rising stars of European mathematics|url=http://www.dw.com/en/dont-call-me-a-prodigy-the-rising-stars-of-european-mathematics/a-19421389|publisher=[[Deutsche Welle]]|accessdate=2016-07-26}}.</ref> She was drawn to mathematics in part because she understood mathematics better than the Swedish language,<ref name="dw"/> and to [[fluid mechanics]] because of its real-world applications.<ref name="em"/> She earned a master's degree from KTH in 2006, and a doctorate in 2011;<ref name="7ecm"/> her dissertation, ''Numerical Methods for Fluid Interface Problems'', was supervised by [[Gunilla Kreiss]].<ref>[http://www.dissertations.se/dissertation/90b61dde41/ ''Numerical Methods for Fluid Interface Problems''], dissertations.se, retrieved 2016-07-26.</ref> After postdoctoral studies at [[Uppsala University]], she returned to KTH as an assistant professor in 2014.<ref name="7ecm"/>
